optimizedDescription.value: Runs trusted graph-index tasks in a lock-owning child with validated IPC, crash containment, typed failures, and deterministic cleanup.

optimizedContext.value:
# Isolated Index Worker

## Rules

- Public `runIsolatedGraphIndex` accepts storage root, trusted installed task-module URL/absolute path, JSON-serializable input, optional progress callback; resolves JSON-serializable result. No rendering, CLI-format interpretation, host exit-state mutation, or `process.exit()`.
- Acquire shared storage-root index lock before fork. Same-root concurrency fails typed busy before second child. Supervisor owns lease through child lifetime; releases exactly once after success, task failure, creation/IPC/send failure, invalid/duplicate terminal IPC, early/non-zero/signal exit, native crash.
- Startup failure bounded without `exit`: detach owned listeners, tear down IPC, best-effort terminate, release once, reject typed startup failure. Lock helpers/tokens remain internal.
- Lock acquisition delegates stale-owner recovery to shared helper from `code-graph:staleness-detection`; supervisor only consumes acquired/typed-busy result; implements no PID recovery.
- Lease-holding process releases on process exit; also Windows `SIGBREAK` and delivered `SIGTERM`. Missing `SIGTERM` delivery MUST NOT leave lease after exit.
- Production uses `node:child_process.fork` with package-shipped worker. Child contains task, parsers, native provider/store work; native crash MUST NOT terminate host. Worker threads/in-process NOT production isolation modes.
- Success requires terminal result, task cleanup, then exit code 0; post-result crash/signal remains failure. Cleanup fixes lifecycle faults without `process.exit()`.
- Worker imports exactly host-selected trusted module. Async task entrypoint receives JSON input, progress emitter, activity announcer (item + optional mandatory flag). Reject missing/non-callable entrypoint or non-serializable input/progress/result as typed task/protocol failure. Task-module selection NOT end-user CLI arg.
- Tagged versioned IPC: progress, activity, one successful terminal, one task-reported failure, malformed/unsupported, exit without terminal. Version MUST change when message types/fields change; mismatch → protocol failure. At most one terminal; duplicate/late → protocol failure, no second settle/release.
- Forward valid progress to optional host callback in arrival order without rendering/lossy transform. No CLI-specific text/JSON/TOON for progress/result.
- Typed failures: busy; fork/IPC startup; invalid task module/contract; task-reported; malformed/unsupported/late/duplicate IPC; non-zero/early exit; signal termination. Post-start failures carry closed `cause`: `start-failed` | `task-contract` | `task-error` | `protocol` | `cancelled` | `native-crash` | `resource-limit` | `exited`. Diagnostics include last activity + stdout/stderr tails. Extend `SpecdCodeGraphError`; stable upper-snake-case codes.
- Capture child stdout/stderr: bounded ≤16 KiB/stream UTF-8 tails; release at end; NEVER write to host streams or forward as progress/events; only in failure diagnostics.
- Activity/silence watchdog (supervisor): rate-limit activity ≤4/s except mandatory; on 10s silence emit `worker-silent` (repeat ≤once/further 10s). MUST NOT terminate child. Throwing event/`onWarning`/string-warning receiver → typed `GraphIndexProgressHandlerError` after child terminate; release lease.
- Optional `onEvent` kinds: `activity`, `worker-silent`, `stale-lock-recovered` (also text via `onWarning`). Arrival order; omit MUST NOT change execution.
- Child runtime: GC request available via fork exec arg; preserve ESM entrypoint args; MUST NOT strip host runtime args.
- Active child: install parent `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` forwarders; remove only installed handlers after terminate; wait, release lock, report signal-derived failure; MUST NOT exit/re-signal host.
- Child receives code-graph-owned indication supervisor holds index lock; provider indexing inside child MUST avoid reacquire. NOT public token; scoped to forked child env.
- Emit stable ESM worker under published `dist/`; resolve relative to installed module location. Built verification: forced project index → terminal result, cleanup, exit 0.
- Cleanup idempotent before promise settles; no leftover lock/child/IPC; detach only installed listeners.

## Constraints

- Only child process provides native-crash containment.
- MUST NOT depend on `@specd/sdk`, `@specd/cli`, Commander, or delivery output formatter.
- Inputs, progress, results, IPC payloads JSON-serializable and runtime-validated at process boundary.
- Direct lock helpers and raw IPC DTOs remain internal.
- No queueing, lock waiting, automatic retry, scheduled/background indexing. No local stale-lock/PID recovery (delegates to `code-graph:staleness-detection` helper).
